extracted.intended_audience: NSF program officers, research administrators, principal investigators, and policy stakeholders interested in merit review metrics and procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts definitions, performance targets, and evaluative metrics used by NSF in describing its merit review process (e.g., funding rates, PI classifications, award types, dwell-time targets, and mechanisms for transformative research). Useful for people preparing proposals, administering awards, or analyzing NSF review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Rate (proposal-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal funding rate: number of awards divided by number of proposals acted on (for the collection of competitively reviewed proposals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout tables and figures (e.g., Table 7). The collection of competitively reviewed proposals includes research proposals, centers and facilities, equipment, instrumentation, conferences and symposia, SBIR, and education and training grants; it excludes preliminary proposals, contracts, IPA agreements, continuing grant increments, Graduate Research Fellowship applications, and similar categories. Funding rates are reported by year and by PI and institutional characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI Funding Rate (three-year window)
rubrics_metrics.description: PI funding rate for a three-year period is defined as the number of investigators receiving a research grant divided by the number of investigators submitting proposals in the same three-year window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to produce the PI funding rate curve (Figure 6). The report notes trends (e.g., temporary increases due to ARRA) and reports PI-level statistics such as average proposals per award and percent of PIs receiving no award in the three-year window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-PI (SPI) vs Multiple-PI (MPI) project metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and funding rates for new research projects with single PIs versus multiple PIs; includes number of projects and total award amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report compares SPI and MPI counts (Figure 2), award amounts in $M (Figure 3), and proposal funding rates (Figure 4). It notes that SPI funding rate has been consistently higher than MPI funding rate and that MPI projects can be associated with multiple awards to different institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Grants per PI
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of the number of research grants held per PI (e.g., percent with one, two, three, four+ grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Averages reported over FY 2016–2018 (Table 5). Example: most PIs (81%) have one research grant; only 4% have three or more grants. Useful for understanding PI workload and award concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of People Supported on Research Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of graduate students, post-doctoral associates, and senior personnel supported on NSF research grants, extracted from grant budget details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 6 reports time series (2008–2018) and percent change. Notes that some individual fellowships are not counted in this research grant category, but most NSF-supported postdocs and grad students are supported as part of research grants. Trends (e.g., peaks due to ARRA) are explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average Number of Months of Budgeted Salary Support per Individual (PI/Co-PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mean number of months of salary support per PI/co-PI in award budgets for single-PI and multiple-PI research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 5 shows trends 2008–2018 and notes directorate-level differences (e.g., ENG awards tend to provide fewer months, ~half the NSF average). Describes historical declines and year-to-year exceptions (FY 2015, FY 2017, FY 2018). Appendix 2 contains directorate-level breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Early Career PI and Later Career PI
rubrics_metrics.description: Early career PI: someone within seven years of receiving his or her last degree at the time of the award. Later career PI: PIs who received their last degree more than seven years before their first NSF award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to report counts, percentages, and funding rates for early vs later career PIs (Figures 7 and 8). The report gives funding-rate comparisons (e.g., later career PIs funding rate 24% vs early career 19% in FY 2018) and percent of awards going to early career PIs (~22%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of New PI
rubrics_metrics.description: A new PI is an individual who has not served as the PI or Co-PI on any award from NSF (with the exception of doctoral dissertation awards, graduate or post-doctoral fellowships, research planning grants, or conferences, symposia and workshop grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition (revised in FY 2009) is used in reporting funding rates and proportions for new PIs (Table 8, Figure 12). The report compares funding rates for new PIs (18%) vs prior PIs (28%) in FY 2018.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive Proposal Inclusion/Exclusion Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: What counts as the universe of 'competitively reviewed proposals' for reporting proposals, awards, and funding rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes research proposals, centers and facilities, equipment, instrumentation, conferences and symposia, SBIR, and education and training grants. Excludes preliminary proposals, contracts, IPA agreements, continuing grant increments, Graduate Research Fellowship applications, and similar categories (footnote 16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Award Mechanisms and Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF uses three funding mechanisms: grants, cooperative agreements, and contracts. Grants may be standard awards or continuing awards (CGIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard awards provide funding for full project duration in a single fiscal year; continuing awards provide annual increments subject to satisfactory progress, funds availability, and required reports. Cooperative agreements require substantial agency involvement; contracts acquire products, services, and studies. Tables show percent of funding by award type (Table 10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Dwell Time (Time to Decision) Performance Goal
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF aim: inform at least 75% of PIs of funding decisions (award or decline) within six months of the proposal deadline, target date, or receipt date, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported dwell-time performance by year (Table 12). The goal was suspended in FY 2009 and FY 2017; FY 2018 result was 72% communicated within six months. Notes about suspension reasons and employee performance plan effects are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms to Encourage Potentially Transformative Research
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF supports potentially transformative research broadly and has specific mechanisms: EAGER, RAPID, RAISE, Creativity Extensions, and Accomplishment-Based Renewals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mechanisms are intended to encourage submissions of high-risk/high-payoff or urgent research and to support interdisciplinary transformative work. Details and Appendix references given; RAISE introduced in NSF 17-1 to encourage transformative interdisciplinary research.

rubrics_metrics.name: EAGER (EArly-concept Grants for Exploratory Research) definition and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: EAGER supports exploratory work on untested but potentially transformative research ideas or approaches (high-risk/high-payoff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests may be for up to $300,000 and up to two years. EAGER replaced SGER (Small Grants for Exploratory Research) and is commonly reviewed internally; program officers may obtain external reviews and will inform the PI if external review will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: RAPID (Grants for Rapid Response Research) definition and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: RAPID is used for proposals with severe urgency regarding availability of data, facilities, or specialized equipment, including quick-response research on disasters and similar unanticipated events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests may be for up to $200,000 and of one year in duration. RAPID proposals are commonly reviewed using only internal reviewers; program officers may choose external review and will notify the PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: EAGER/RAPID Review Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: EAGER and RAPID proposals are commonly reviewed using only internal reviewers; program officers may elect external review and must inform the PI if external review will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains variability in review path and that program officers have discretion to seek external input. Appendix 7 provides award counts by directorate and usage patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and Distribution of SGER/EAGER/RAPID Awards by Directorate
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and directorate-level variation in use of SGER (historical), EAGER, and RAPID awards (Figure 14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is considerable variation across directorates: CISE and ENG received far more EAGER proposals in recent years; RAPID proposals are proportionally more common in GEO. Appendix 7 contains further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outreach Activities to Increase Participation and Success
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF conducts outreach (grants conference, 'NSF Days', informational booths at meetings, directorate workshops) to help increase participation and success in NSF programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: one in-person Grants Conference (two-day, ~25 NSF reps), four NSF Days in FY 2018, and presence at meetings for under-represented groups (SACNAS, AISES, ABRCMS). Program officers conduct outreach during visits and conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPSCoR Mission and Geographic Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: EPSCoR (Established Program to Stimulate Competitive Research) mission: strengthen research and education throughout the U.S. and avoid undue concentration of research and education, targeting jurisdictions with historically lesser NSF R&D funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In FY 2018, 24 states plus Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, and Guam were eligible for aspects of EPSCoR. Appendix 5 provides EPSCoR proposal/award/funding-rate data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of Funds by Type of Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages of NSF program funds awarded by sector: academic institutions, non-profit/other organizations, for-profit businesses, Federally Funded R&D Centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 11 reports time series (2008–2018). Example FY 2018: ~77% to academic institutions, 11% to non-profit/other, 8% to for-profit, 4% to FFRDCs. Notes on category reclassifications (FY 2015) are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Funding Rates by Type of Academic Institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal funding rates reported for institution categories (e.g., Top 100 Ph.D.-granting institutions, Ph.D.-granting not Top 100, four-year institutions, two-year institutions, minority-serving institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example FY 2018 rates: Top 100 Ph.D.-granting = 27%; Ph.D.-granting not Top 100 = 18%; four-year = 29%; two-year = 35%; minority-serving institutions = 23%. Used to monitor institutional disparities in funding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of Participation Metrics (gender, race/ethnicity, disability, new/prior PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF tracks proposals, awards, and funding rates by proposer characteristics: gender, under-represented racial/ethnic group membership, disability, and new/prior PI status. Data are largely self-reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report notes response rates (e.g., ~84% provided gender, ~83% race, ~82% ethnicity, ~67% disability). Tables and figures (Table 8, Figures 9–11) show counts and funding rates. Footnotes explain estimation methods where reporting is incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Under-Represented Racial or Ethnic Groups (URMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under-represented ethnic/racial PIs category includes American Indian/Alaska Native, Black/African American, Hispanic or Latino, and Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander; it does not include non-Hispanic Asian or White PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for reporting proposals/awards and funding rates. The report notes that representation among PIs is lower than U.S. population but similar to representation among full-time faculty in relevant fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Race/Ethnicity Reporting and Multiracial Category
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning in FY 2012, individuals identifying race and Hispanic/Latino are included in both the racial group and Hispanic/Latino; a multiracial category was added. Prior reporting treated Hispanic/Latino differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote explains the change and that small counts (e.g., American Indian/Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander) lead to greater year-to-year funding-rate fluctuations. Appendix and figure notes describe estimation methods for earlier years when data were incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Rate for PIs with Disabilities (PWDs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal funding rate for PIs identifying themselves as having a disability is tracked and reported; in FY 2018 it was ~1% higher than overall funding rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 11 and Table 8 provide counts and funding rates. Notes that ~67% of competitively reviewed proposals included disability status reporting, and ~1.4% of those reported having a disability in FY 2018.
